name: @wirl/mcp

tools.name: wirl_login
tools.description: Sign this machine in to wirl so the other wirl tools work. Use this the first time, or whenever another wirl tool says it is not signed in. It returns a link and a short code: show both to the person, ask them to open the link and approve, then retry whatever you were doing. Nothing to paste back — the token is saved for you once they approve.

tools.name: wirl_deploy
tools.description: Deploy a directory of files to a URL that colleagues can open. Use this when the user has built something — a dashboard, a report, an internal tool — and wants it somewhere real instead of on their laptop. A new app is visible to everyone in the org when the org came from a company email domain; in any other org, including a personal one or one made with wirl orgs create, it starts private. Either way, share it by email to add someone outside that. Returns the URL, and who can open the app as the edge has it when the deploy finishes (a visibility change made while it ran included). Creates the app on first deploy. A wirl.json beside or inside the directory declares a "server" module for a backend and any "connections" the app needs; the answer says which declared connections are usable now, which are waiting on an admin and which need a key, and names the flows the version declares. New files in migrations/ are applied to the app's database before the version goes live; one that fails fails the deploy, and the version already live, if any, keeps serving. A destructive file (one wirl.json's "destructive" list must name) waits for a person before it applies to the live database: the refusal gives the address of the page where they approve it, and nothing this tool takes skips that. A declared name the org already has is that connection, not a new one: the answer names who made it, whether it holds a key and the other apps you can open that use it. Declaring a kind it does not have is refused, unless a deploy, never a preview, may change it: it has no key, you made it or are an org admin, no other app is granted it, and neither kind is webhook_secret. Refuses, without uploading anything, if the directory contains what looks like a live API key or password. A preview takes a version number from the same count as a deploy, and wirl_list_versions never lists a preview, so a deploy's number can skip: if the newest version listed is v1 and this deploy is v4, v2 and v3 were previews.

directory.description: Path to the folder to deploy. Usually the build output, e.g. ./dist

app.description: App name, lowercase with hyphens, e.g. "quarterly-dashboard". Becomes part of the URL. Defaults to "app" in the project's wirl.json, else the folder's name.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_preview
tools.description: Put a directory of files up as a preview: a version of an app that is never live, at its own address, with its own database (every file in migrations/ applied, and no rows but the ones those files insert, the first time that name is used), open to the same people who can already open the app. Use this to preview before deploying — before wirl_deploy, whenever a change has not been checked yet — then look at what it actually rendered with wirl_preview_fetch instead of asking the person to open a link and describe what they see. It uses the app's real connections (as wirl_deploy's does, the answer says which declared connections are usable now, which are waiting on an admin and which need a key, and names the flows the build declares), but its own database starts with no rows but the ones the files in migrations/ insert, and its schedules do not run on a clock, so a page that expects rows may look blank until something writes to it. A declared name the org already has is that connection, not a new one: the answer names who made it, whether it holds a key and the other apps you can open that use it. Declaring a kind it does not have is refused, unless a deploy, never a preview, may change it: it has no key, you made it or are an org admin, no other app is granted it, and neither kind is webhook_secret. An app holds at most 5 previews at once; a sixth is refused until one is deleted with wirl_delete_preview. Each one expires after 14 days if not redeployed. Deploying a preview again under its name replaces its build: wirl_logs with preview then reads only the new build's lines, and the earlier build's are no longer shown. Refuses, without uploading anything, if the directory contains what looks like a live API key or password. Works for a new app too: the app is made if it is not there yet, and its own address answers 404 until wirl_deploy.

directory.description: Path to the folder to preview. Usually the build output, e.g. ./dist

name.description: The preview's name, becoming the third part of its address (org--app--name). Defaults to the current git branch (unless it is main, master or HEAD), else the part of the signed-in email before the @.

app.description: The app slug this previews. Defaults to "app" in the project's wirl.json, else the folder's name.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_list_connections
tools.description: List the connections in the organisation: named credentials an app may be granted, such as a HubSpot or Stripe key, with the hosts each allows, who made each (by name and email) and whether it holds its key, is waiting for one, or needs none. Use this to learn the exact name to put under "connections" in wirl.json before deploying an app that needs one; a name already listed here is that connection, not a new one, and other apps may be granted it too. The app never receives the key: it calls the vendor's own real URL (fetch("https://api.hubspot.com/...")) and wirl attaches the key on the way out. Declaring one at deploy grants it at once only when you made it or are an org admin, signed in with full access, it was never revoked from that app, and no request for it is already waiting; otherwise, unless the app already holds it, it opens or keeps a request that its maker or an org admin approves. There is no tool to approve one.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_share
tools.description: Give a named colleague access to a deployed app, by email address. Use this when the user says someone should be able to see what they built. Access belongs to that person and can be taken back. Viewers are free — sharing never costs anything, so there is no reason to hesitate. Role "viewer" can open it; "editor" can also deploy to it. Sharing again with no role keeps the role a person has: pass "role" only to give or change one, and the answer says what the role is and, when it changed one, what it was. A connection with deploy-only access cannot share; if the server says so, tell the person to open the app's Access page in the dashboard instead.

email.description: Work email address of the person.

role.description: Leave it out unless the person should be given or moved to a role: a new person is a viewer, and someone who already has access, or is already invited, keeps the role they have. Naming one sets it, lowering an editor to viewer included.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

annotations.title: Share an app with a person

tools.name: wirl_pull
tools.description: Fetch the source of a deployed app into a local directory, to change it and deploy again. Use this when the user wants to work on an app a colleague built and shared with them, or to recover the source of one of their own. Anyone who can open the app can pull it. Refuses a directory that already has files in it unless told to overwrite.

directory.description: Where to put it. Defaults to a directory named after the app.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

overwrite.description: Allow a directory that is not empty. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wirl_unshare
tools.description: Take back a named person's access to a deployed app, by the email address it was shared with. Use this when the user says someone should no longer see what they built. It takes the whole share away, one person at a time; to change a role instead, use wirl_share with "role". It also withdraws an invitation that is still waiting for an address, and works while the app is deleted and can still be restored. It says what it found; finding nothing is not an error. Needs a sign-in with full access, like wirl_share.

email.description: The email address the app was shared with.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_visibility
tools.description: See or change who can open an app. With no level it only reports the current one. "private": only its owner, the organisation's owners and admins, and the people it is shared with by email. "org": everyone signed in at the organisation. Use this when the person says who the app is for ("only me", "just my team and whoever I share it with", "the whole company"). It cannot make an app public, and nothing an agent can call can: anyone on the internet being able to open it is a decision a person takes with their own click, on the app's Access page in the dashboard, so if they ask for that, give them that link. To give one named person access use wirl_share instead. A connection with deploy-only access cannot change this either; if the server says so, send the person to the same Access page.

level.description: Leave it out to see the current level without changing anything.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

annotations.title: See or set who can open an app

tools.name: wirl_list_apps
tools.description: List the apps the user can open, with their URLs and who can see them. Use this to find an app before deploying to it or sharing it, or when the user asks what they have already deployed.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_list_versions
tools.description: List past deployments of an app, newest first, with their version numbers and ids. Use this before rolling back, to find which version to return to. A preview takes a version number from the same sequence and is never listed here, so the numbers can skip: a first deploy after one preview is v2.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_rollback
tools.description: Put an earlier deployment back to being the live one. Use this when a deploy broke something and the user wants the previous version back. Instant — nothing is rebuilt. Get the deployment id from wirl_list_versions first.

deployment_id.description: The deployment to make live again. Get it from wirl_list_versions.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_migrations
tools.description: List what one of an app's databases has applied, read only: its own record of migrations (_wirl_migrations), read now, and wirl's ledger of what it sent there, one line a file, saying where the two differ. Use this before changing anything when a deploy was refused over a migration, or said it could not tell whether a file applied. It writes nothing, and needs the access a deploy needs.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

preview.description: A preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), to read that preview's database instead of the live one.

tools.name: wirl_list_schedules
tools.description: List an app's schedules (from its wirl.json) with the last run's outcome and the next run time. Use this to see whether a scheduled job is healthy.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_run
tools.description: Run one of an app's schedules right now and wait for the outcome (up to the schedule's timeout). Use this after deploying a schedule to check it works, instead of waiting for the clock. With `preview`, runs one of a preview's own schedules instead: it must be declared in the previewed wirl.json (a preview writes no schedule rows, so nothing of its fires on a clock), and the outcome comes back at once, with no queue to wait on.

schedule.description: The schedule's name, from wirl.json or wirl_list_schedules.

preview.description: Run this schedule against a preview instead of the live app, by the preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews).

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_list_flows
tools.description: List the flows an app declares under "flows" in its wirl.json, each with its step timeout, its retries, how many of its runs are unfinished and its last run. Use this to find a flow's exact name before wirl_start_flow, or to see whether runs are piling up. With preview, lists what that preview's own build declares instead of the live app's.

preview.description: A preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), for its flows and runs instead of the live app's. Leave it out for the live app.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_start_flow
tools.description: Start a run of one of an app's flows. Use this to try a flow you have built: put it up with wirl_preview, start it here with preview and fast (fast, for a preview's run only, makes each sleep, until and retry delay the flow asks for 5 seconds, each wait's timeout 60 seconds, and each retry of a failing step 10 seconds, 90 after a try that ran out of time; wirl_retry_run still refuses a failed run until 4 minutes after it failed), follow it with wirl_show_run, answer each wait it reaches with wirl_send_event, and read what each step printed with wirl_logs with the run's id, and with preview for a preview's run. A key names the run in the app's own terms: starting the flow again with the same key finds the run it started instead of starting another, until 30 days after that run ends, so give each new try a new key. The input is at most 64 KiB: keep rows in env.DB and pass ids. Where flows are not on for the organisation yet, the answer says so and nothing starts.

flow.description: The flow's name, from wirl.json or wirl_list_flows.

input.description: The run's input: any JSON value, at most 64 KiB, passed as the value itself (an object, say), not as JSON text: text is a string input, so input.orderId would read undefined. Left out, the run starts with null.

key.description: The app's own name for the run, unique among the target's runs: 1 to 100 letters, digits, dots, colons, dashes or underscores, not starting with run_ or schedule:, which are wirl's. It names that run until 30 days after the run ends, on a preview deployed again or made anew too, so give each new try a new key.

preview.description: Start the run on this preview, by the preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), instead of the live app.

fast.description: A preview's run only: each sleep, until and retry delay the flow asks for becomes 5 seconds, each wait's timeout 60 seconds, and each retry of a failing step waits 10 seconds (90 after a try that ran out of time). wirl_retry_run still refuses a failed run until 4 minutes after it failed.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_list_runs
tools.description: List an app's flow runs, newest first, each with its status, the step it is at and when it started. Use this to find a run to look at with wirl_show_run, or to see which runs failed or are waiting. Narrow it with flow and status. A preview's runs are listed only with preview, and the live app's only without it.

flow.description: Only the runs of this flow.

status.description: Only the runs with this status.

limit.description: At most this many runs, 1 to 100. Default 20.

preview.description: A preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), for its flows and runs instead of the live app's. Leave it out for the live app.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_show_run
tools.description: Show one flow run: its status, who started it, what it waits for or sleeps until or, while wirl is still creating it, when wirl tries again, the step it goes on with next and since or from when (a step reports only when it ends, so one that is running says it has not reported yet), its output or error, its page on the dashboard, its newest 50 attempts with the version of the app that answered each and each attempt's deadline, and the earlier attempts that went wrong, and its newest 50 events with who sent each and whether it reached the run (the run's page lists every one). Use this after wirl_start_flow to follow a run step by step, and to learn which event a waiting run asks for before wirl_send_event. A preview's run is found only with preview, and a live run only without it.

run.description: The run's id (run_...), or the key it was started with.

preview.description: A preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), for its flows and runs instead of the live app's. Leave it out for the live app.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_send_event
tools.description: Answer what a preview's run waits for: send it the event its wait asks for, with an optional JSON object as the event's body. Use this to walk a flow through its waits while trying it on a preview, once wirl_show_run says which event the run waits for. The event is sent as you, so its from.email is your own address, and an app that takes a decision only from people it lists takes yours only if you are listed; to try that path, list yourself in the build you preview, and never loosen the check. It is for a preview's runs only: a live run is answered by a person, on the app's own page or the run's page on the dashboard, so this refuses a live run before sending anything and says where the person goes. Only a wait open for that event takes it, and only the first answer to a wait counts.

run.description: The run's id (run_...), or the key it was started with.

event.description: The name of the event the run waits for, as wirl_show_run shows it.

data.description: The event's body, a JSON object of at most 64 KiB. Left out, it is {}.

preview.description: The preview the run is on, by the preview's name. Without it the run is a live one, which only a person answers.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

annotations.title: Answer a wait on a preview run

tools.name: wirl_cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel a flow run: a step already running is stopped where it is. Use this when a run is stuck, was started by mistake, or is doing the wrong thing. A run that had already finished is left as it is, and the answer says so. A preview's run is found only with preview, and a live run only without it.

run.description: The run's id (run_...), or the key it was started with.

preview.description: A preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), for its flows and runs instead of the live app's. Leave it out for the live app.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_retry_run
tools.description: Run a failed flow run again, from the step it failed at, or from an earlier step with from. Use this when what made the run fail has passed, such as a vendor that was down, or once a fix is deployed live, rather than starting a new run. A run can be retried from four minutes after it failed until three days after, while Cloudflare still keeps it; outside that the answer says why. A preview's failed run cannot be retried once the preview has been deployed again or removed, or has expired: start a new run. A preview's run is found only with preview, and a live run only without it. Where flows are not on for the organisation yet, the answer says so.

run.description: The run's id (run_...), or the key it was started with.

from.description: The number of the step to run again from, as wirl_show_run's attempts number them (n). Left out, the step the run failed at.

preview.description: A preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews), for its flows and runs instead of the live app's. Leave it out for the live app.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_logs
tools.description: What a deployed app printed, grouped per request (page load, webhook, schedule run, flow step), newest first, with the status and any exception. Use this first when a deploy misbehaves, a schedule or webhook failed, or someone reports an error, before changing code. Defaults to the last hour. A line usually appears within a minute of the request, not at once; if the run you expect is missing, wait and read again. With `preview`, reads that preview's own script instead of the live app's history. Logs are what the app printed, as far as Cloudflare kept them: Workers Logs can miss a request's lines, all of them at times. A run's record is wirl_show_run and the run's page, not its logs: never count a run's steps from them.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

since.description: How far back: "15m", "1h", "24h", "7d" or an ISO time. Default "1h".

errors_only.description: Only invocations that failed or printed at error level.

kind.description: Only one kind of request: a page load, a webhook, a schedule run, a flow's step, or other.

run.description: Only the invocations of this run: a flow run's id (from wirl_start_flow or wirl_list_runs), each of whose steps is one invocation, or a schedule run id (from wirl_run or wirl_list_schedules). A preview's run needs preview as well, since its steps ran on the preview's own script.

ray.description: Only the request with this cf-ray id, as read off a response header.

search.description: Only invocations whose path or printed text contains this text (not a stack, nor fields logged beside a line), or whose status it is (three digits, such as 404). At most 1,024 bytes. It never searches who made a request.

limit.description: At most this many invocations, 1 to 200. Default 50.

cursor.description: From a previous answer's 'More before this' line, to read the page before it.

preview.description: Read this preview's own script instead of the live app, by the preview's name (from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews). Its current build only: once the preview is deployed again, the earlier build's lines are not shown.

tools.name: wirl_egress
tools.description: What a deployed app called out through wirl, call by call, newest first: when, the method and host, the connection, the status, and allowed or the code wirl refused it with; a flow step's call also names its run, step number n and attempt, and the path it called, never its query string. No header or body is recorded. Use this to check which calls a page, a schedule or a flow step actually made to a vendor, or why one was refused, before changing code: two calls of a retried step differ by attempt. Defaults to the last hour, at most seven days back. A flow step's call refused because its deadline had passed is not recorded. Only the app's own calls, for someone who can deploy it, as its logs are.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

since.description: How far back: "15m", "1h", "24h", "7d" or an ISO time. Default "1h", and never more than seven days.

run.description: Only this run's calls: a flow run's id (from wirl_start_flow or wirl_list_runs), each call with its step's n and attempt, or a schedule run id.

limit.description: At most this many calls, 1 to 200. Default 50.

cursor.description: From a previous answer's 'More before this' line, to read the page before it.

tools.name: wirl_list_previews
tools.description: List an app's previews: folders put up at their own address, never live, each with its own database (its tables from migrations/, and at first no rows but the ones those files insert). Use this to find a preview's exact name before calling wirl_preview_fetch or wirl_delete_preview, or to see when one expires. An app holds at most 5 previews at once, each for up to 14 days unless redeployed.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_preview_fetch
tools.description: Make one request to a preview and show what it answers: the status, the content type, and the body as text — the page source for HTML, so you can see what the app actually rendered and fix it. Use this after wirl_preview instead of asking the person to open the link and describe what they see. A binary body reports its type and size, not its bytes. A text body over 100 KB is cut, and the answer says so. A stream (server-sent events, newline-delimited JSON, or any text still arriving after 10 seconds) is shown with the time each line arrived, as far as it got, and says whether it was still going: that is how to check a stream arrives piece by piece. A stream also comes back as data, in the result's structuredContent: the same lines as { atMs, text }, atMs being whole milliseconds from sending the request to the read that completed the line (lines that arrived together share one), the first 2,000 lines or 16 KB of their text, whichever comes first (always at least the first line), with linesLeftOut counting any more (the text shows them all), and the status, the content type and the flags stillStreaming, bodyComplete, truncated and lastLineEnded; any other answer is the text alone. A preview's own database starts with the tables in migrations/ and no rows but the ones those files insert, so a page that expects rows may look blank until something writes to it, and its schedules do not run on a clock. A 401, or a redirect back to sign in, means the visit was refused or the preview has expired or been deleted, not that the app itself answered that way. The headers argument cannot set host, cookie, content-length, or any x-wirl-* header (including x-wirl-visit): those are wirl's own, and are dropped rather than sent. This tool cannot send a file or save an answer as bytes: body is sent as text, exactly as given (an @ in it is just a character), and a binary answer reports only its type and size. From a shell, wirl fetch --data @file sends a file and --output <file> saves the answer, each up to 100,000,000 bytes.

app.description: The app slug the preview belongs to.

name.description: The preview's name, from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews.

path.description: The path to request, e.g. "/" or "/api/notes".

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to GET, or POST when a body is given.

headers.description: Extra request headers, as {"header-name": "value"}. host, cookie, content-length and any x-wirl-* header are not yours to set and are dropped.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

annotations.title: Request a page from a preview

tools.name: wirl_delete_preview
tools.description: Remove a preview: its script, its files, its database and its address all go away. Use this to free a slot when an app already has 5 previews (the most it can hold at once) and a new one is needed, or when a preview is no longer wanted before its own expiry. Idempotent: deleting one already gone still succeeds.

app.description: The app slug the preview belongs to.

name.description: The preview's name, from wirl_preview or wirl_list_previews.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_delete_app
tools.description: Delete an app. Use this only when the person has asked for this app to be deleted; to try something, use wirl_preview. It is a soft delete: the app's address and its previews stop answering at once, its schedules stop and its unfinished runs are cancelled, and its data is kept for 30 days. Until then its owner, while a member of the organisation, or an organisation owner or admin can bring it back with wirl apps restore <app> --org <org>, or from the Recently deleted list on the organisation's tools page in the dashboard; an app that was public comes back only from that list. Its name stays taken for good. Needs a full-scope sign-in: a deploy-scoped token is refused, with where to do it instead.

app.description: The slug of the app to delete. Always named: never guessed from a folder.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

tools.name: wirl_whoami
tools.description: Show which account this session is signed in as and which organisations it belongs to. Use this to check the connection works, or to find an organisation slug.

tools.name: wirl_migrations_adopt
tools.description: Move an app whose own code made its tables onto migrations, once: the shape of the app's live database (its tables, views and indexes, never a row) becomes migrations/0001_init.sql in the folder that holds wirl.json, recorded as applied on the live database. Use this before the first migration of an app already on wirl that made its tables in code: until then a deploy with files in migrations/ is refused. Refused while migrations/ holds any .sql file. The project's .wirl/local.sqlite is recorded too when it has the same shape and no record of other files, so wirl dev keeps its rows. Pointed at build output, it writes beside the wirl.json next to it, and the build must copy migrations/ to the top of what it deploys. Adopting again replaces the record of an earlier adopt, and is refused once a later file has applied.

directory.description: The project folder, the one holding wirl.json (or its build output, beside it).

app.description: The app slug. Defaults to "app" in the project's wirl.json, else the folder's name.

org.description: Organisation slug. Optional when the person belongs to only one; otherwise the tool says which ones exist and asks.

instructions:
wirl deploys a small internal tool to a URL colleagues can open, with company sign-in, a database and vaulted API keys already wired up.
Reach for it whenever what you just built should live somewhere shared instead of only on this machine.
The text below writes a command as `wirl <command>` for short; run one as `npx wirl <command>`, which needs no install beyond Node 22.13 or later.

A wirl app is a folder of static files, or one JavaScript or TypeScript module exporting
`fetch(request, env)`, named by `server` in `wirl.json`. No other language, no long-running process, no
disk, no build step: deploy built output. Responses stream as the module sends them, so server-sent events
work, and a vendor's event stream (`text/event-stream`, `application/x-ndjson`) reaches the module as it
arrives: pass `response.body` straight on. There are no WebSockets. A front end goes beside the module:
`"static": "dist"` serves that folder's files at their own paths (`/` is its `index.html`) and the module
answers everything else; add `"spa": true` for a client-side router. Nothing outside that folder is served.

Preview before you deploy: `wirl preview` gives a folder its own address and database (at first only what
`migrations/` makes). `wirl fetch <path> --preview <name>` or `wirl_preview_fetch` shows what it answers. Every request a preview's module gets names the preview in `x-wirl-preview`, and wirl marks its pages as previews.

npm packages work: install them in the project and the deploy bundles them in. Nothing is installed on the
server: native code will not run. Node built-ins work (`node:crypto`, `node:path`, ...; `Buffer` and
`process` are global), but what `node:fs` writes is gone by the next request: use `env.DB`.

`env` holds `DB` and nothing else. `env.DB` is Cloudflare D1: prepared statements with `.bind()`, at most
100 bound parameters a statement. `exec()` runs one statement per line, as does each file in `migrations/`,
which wirl applies in order to a preview and before going live; a failing one fails the deploy. Never edit
an applied file. Dropping or renaming a table or column needs `"migrations": { "destructive": [...] }`, its
own live deploy and a person's yes. Declare a host under `connections`, then `fetch` the vendor's real URL:
wirl attaches the key. An undeclared host is refused; a public API needing no key uses `"kind": "none"`.
Declaring one deploys before anyone approves it; the deploy says per connection whether it is usable now or
waiting on an admin. A vendor has 60 seconds to answer, whole, unless it streams: ask a model for a stream.

Six headers say who is asking: `x-wirl-user-id`, `x-wirl-user-email`, `x-wirl-user-name`,
`x-wirl-role`, `x-wirl-app-id`, `x-wirl-org`. Read the name with
`decodeURIComponent(request.headers.get("x-wirl-user-name") || "")`. The first four are empty for an
anonymous visitor, a schedule run, a flow step, or a public path; the last two are always set.
Schedules POST to `/__wirl/schedule/<name>`; a run gets 5 minutes unless that schedule's own `timeout`
says otherwise, and at most 15. A `public_paths` path takes requests with no sign-in.
Work that outlives one request (waiting for a person, trying tomorrow, a long loop) is a flow: see Flows.

A new app defaults to org-wide visibility when its org has a company email domain, and to private
otherwise, including one made with `wirl orgs create`; `wirl visibility private|org` sets the level.
Sharing by email adds one named person. Public is only ever a person's click on the app's Access page.

Porting an existing project: route it through the `fetch` handler, replace ORM calls with
`env.DB.prepare(...).bind(...)`, turn timers into `schedules`, and move keys into `connections`. Keep the
front end: build it, and name the build folder under `static`. Say in one sentence what you are changing.

## Flows

Declare `"flows": [{ "name": "refund", "step_timeout": "5m", "retries": 5 }]`. wirl POSTs each step to
`/__wirl/flow/<name>` as JSON `{ run, step, n, attempt, input, state, event }`: `step` is "start" first,
`input` comes every time, and nobody is signed in (put who asked in `input`). Answer 200 with
`{ "next": "<step>", "state": {...} }`, plus `"sleep": "1d"`, `"until": "<ISO time>"` or
`"wait": { "event": "<name>", "timeout": "3d", "otherwise": "<step>" }`: `next` gets the event as `event`,
with `from.email` set by wirl (null for no person, never an approver), or `otherwise` (required) runs at
the timeout. `{ "retry": "1d", "state": {...} }` runs the step again later (same `n`, next `attempt`),
`{ "fail": "why" }` stops the run, and `{ "done": true, "output": {...} }` finishes it. `state` is only
what an answer sends, so send it with every `next` and `retry`: ids, never rows or secrets, in an answer
under 1 MiB. A throw is a blip, retried from 10 s to 6 h, `retries` times; for "tomorrow", answer `retry`.
A step is cancelled at its `step_timeout`, its outgoing calls (`ctx.waitUntil`'s too) refused 5 s after,
yet can run twice, even beside a timed-out try of itself, and a retried run runs its steps again under the
same keys: upsert, and give a vendor an `Idempotency-Key` named for the operation. Refuse a call whose
`x-wirl-flow` is not that name (only wirl sets it), and answer `fail` to a step you don't know. A run that
fails or is cancelled ends with one more call, step "failed" or "cancelled", with a `reason` (its `n` may
be a step's too; state null on cancel; none if its code is gone); the answer is ignored. Give each wait its
own name, ask the same thing on every try (an answer can reach a later one), and have an approval name what
it approves to check against `state`. A deploy between steps runs new code on old `state`. Test in a
preview with `wirl flows start --fast`: previews share pools (10,000 steps a day, each try counted, 10 at
once, 1,000 unfinished runs) a loop can use up, never live's. `https://flows.wirl` needs no connection:
`POST /flows/<name>` with `{ input, key }` starts a run, never fast (`{ run }`; a `key` gets its run until
30 days after it ends); `POST /runs/<run or key>/events/<name>` with a JSON object answers an open wait (an
early, repeated or late one gets 409, or 404 once the run ends; check `x-wirl-user-email` first);
`GET /runs/<run or key>` is its status (a null `output` with `outputTruncated: true` was cut at 64 KiB).
